items.headline: HBM capacity (third-party est.): Korean industry sources say Micron is pulling forward HBM equipment orders, mainly Hanmi TC bonders, for Singapore and Taiwan; its ~$7B Singapore HBM packaging plant (first tool-in 19 Nov) targets initial output in early 2027. Estimates put Micron's HBM wafer input at ~100k wafers/month by end-2026 (about double a year earlier, ~half of Samsung's or SK hynix's); Counterpoint puts Q2 2026 HBM share at SK hynix 50%, Samsung 33%, Micron 18% (Chosun Biz (industry sources; Counterpoint est.), 2026-11-24)

Competitors (24 Nov, Asia): SK hynix traded ~12% higher (₩1.217M) and Samsung Electronics ~10% higher (₩194,700) in Korean pre-market trading after Huang's return, following a 23 Nov KOSPI close of −3.31% (Samsung −3.06%, SK hynix −2.52%, both at their lowest closes since March–April); KOSPI 200 night futures rose 7.06% (Chosun Biz; Yonhap, 2026-11-24)
MU closed $707.70 on 2026-11-23, -1.6% vs $719.02 on 2026-11-16 (Nasdaq.com official closes)

MU jumped 19.04% on 23 Nov to close at $707.70 (from $594.51; range $666.66–$720.69, ~49M shares, ~72% above its 3-month average), ending a seven-session losing streak, after Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO and Citi called the memory sell-off overdone; PHLX Semiconductor index +14.03%, Nasdaq Composite +6.51% (best day since April 2025), S&P 500 +4.73%; Nvidia +31.48%, SK hynix ADR +20.00%, Dell +20.46%, Western Digital +13.84%. MU last traded ~$705 (−0.4%) after hours (Nasdaq.com) (Nasdaq.com; The Motley Fool; CNBC, 2026-11-23)

Asia open (23 Nov): Samsung Electronics (−5.4%, ₩173,200) and SK hynix (−5.8%, ₩1.05M) fell in Korean pre-market trading after the 20 Nov US chip rout, in which SK hynix's US ADR fell 13.11% and KOSPI night futures 7.0%; Seoul readied its ₩10.76T market-stabilisation fund, eased buyback order caps for three months from 24 Nov and stepped up illegal short-selling checks (no short-sale ban) (Seoul Economic Daily; Aju Press; Hankyung, 2026-11-23)

Largest HBM customer: Nvidia's board unanimously reinstated Jensen Huang as president, CEO and director with immediate effect, 11 days after he resigned, saying it received input from senior US government officials and is confident his return poses no national-security risk; the independent directors' investigation continues with his cooperation. Nvidia rose 31.48%, regaining nearly $1 trillion in market value; President Trump said Nvidia's internal export-control compliance review should continue (NVIDIA Newsroom; AP, 2026-11-23)

Memory cost pass-through: the FT reports Dell, HPE, Lenovo and Supermicro are seeking AI-server price increases of up to 45% after contracts were signed, mainly because of memory costs; GPU server prices are up at least 20–30% and CPU server nodes have more than tripled. HPE says it now lets orders be repriced if component costs rise and expects high memory and storage prices well into 2027 (TrendForce (citing Financial Times), 2026-11-23)

HBM demand debate (third-party est.): SemiAnalysis reportedly cut its 2028 global HBM bit-demand forecast by ~30% and its 2028 AI-accelerator spending forecast to $758B from $1.054T; KB Securities sees 2027 HBM demand split Nvidia 38%, Google 37%, AMD 13%. SK hynix's largest customer (presumed Nvidia) fell to 14.8% of its 9M 2026 sales from 27% a year earlier; Samsung and SK hynix filings note contract volumes can change with customer demand (Korea JoongAng Daily (KB Securities, SemiAnalysis estimates), 2026-11-22)

Bear view (third-party opinion): Objective Analysis founder Jim Handy told The Korea Times the memory price surge is 'temporary' and that hyperscalers spending ~40% of revenue on capex are likely to slow at some point, which would cause memory prices to collapse, possibly back to 2024 levels; he did not give a timing (The Korea Times, 2026-11-22)

Analyst note (Citi, third-party est.): Atif Malik reiterated Buy and a $1,300 target, calling the memory sell-off overdone; Citi estimates that even if Nvidia-related financing (~14% of hyperscaler capex by its assumption) stopped completely, total DRAM demand would fall only ~12% and NAND ~7%, and expects DRAM and HBM supply to stay constrained through 2027–28, with tighter US equipment curbs limiting bit growth at China fabs (Investing.com; GuruFocus; TipRanks, 2026-11-22)

Largest HBM customer: The New York Times reported on 21 Nov that the SEC's inquiry into Nvidia's accounting is at an early stage and may end without charges; its focus is unconfirmed, and reports note Nvidia's 2025 switch to reporting regional sales by customer headquarters, which removed Singapore from its breakdown. Nvidia and the SEC have not commented; Bloomberg separately reports California's attorney general says his probe also covers potential criminal violations of state law (AFP (via France 24); The New York Times, 2026-11-21)

MU fell 13.89% on 20 Nov to close at $594.51 (from $690.44; opened $665.46, range $585.25–$669.00, ~59.4M shares per Nasdaq.com), its seventh straight decline, lowest close since 4 May 2026 and ~23.6% down on the week, now ~51% below its 25 Jun record, in a broad AI-chip sell-off (PHLX Semiconductor index −10.73%, Nasdaq Composite −5.28%, S&P 500 −3.70% and in correction territory; Nvidia −14%, SanDisk −16%, Western Digital −12%). MU last traded $610.60 (+2.7%) in after-hours (StockAnalysis, 7:59 pm ET) (Nasdaq.com historical; AP; StockAnalysis, 2026-11-20)

Competitors: SoftBank's Masayoshi Son approached Wall Street institutions about financing a possible ~$1 trillion buyout of SK hynix (The Information); SoftBank says the idea is 'no longer under active consideration', and SK hynix says it has no knowledge of it and that any foreign acquisition would need Korean government approval (Reuters (via CNA), citing The Information, 2026-11-20)

Largest HBM customer: Nvidia fell 14% to $125.53 on 20 Nov (−23% on the week, its worst since 2008) after Reuters reported that SEC enforcement staff are examining potential accounting issues at the company; the SEC declined to comment and an investigation does not establish wrongdoing. The stock is ~48% below its 6 Oct record despite the FQ3 beat and $130B FQ4 guide (Reuters (via Investing.com), 2026-11-20)

Demand outlook (TrendForce, third-party est., 20 Nov): Chinese CSPs have scaled back purchases of enterprise SSDs and some server DRAM; TrendForce keeps its overall 2027 DRAM demand outlook unchanged and says DRAM stays undersupplied but with price increases narrowing each quarter, while NAND tips into oversupply earlier than expected, slowing 2027 memory revenue growth (TrendForce (research summary), 2026-11-20)

Hyperscaler AI chips (third-party est.): analyst Ming-Chi Kuo says his survey shows Google cut planned 2027 shipments of the Broadcom-designed TPU 8i series by ~1M units (~20%), mostly the pricier 8i Max, while planning more MediaTek-designed TPU 8t units; he ties it to frontier-model compute priority and power limits rather than a pullback. Broadcom fell ~11%; neither company commented (Investing.com (Ming-Chi Kuo, TF International), 2026-11-20)

Asia memory sell-off (20 Nov): KOSPI −5.21% with Samsung Electronics −7.01% and SK hynix −5.92% as Anthropic's debut failed to ease AI-spending worries (Yonhap); Kioxia fell 11.66% in Tokyo after guiding Oct–Dec revenue only ~1% q/q higher on flat shipments, while saying its 2027 capacity is largely sold out (GuruFocus) (Yonhap; GuruFocus, 2026-11-20)

Valuation debate: MarketWatch puts MU at 3.76x next-12-month EPS vs a two-year average of 9.10x; Futurum's Brendan Burke calls low memory P/Es 'a warning label, not a bargain sign' (though AI may make earnings more durable) and CreditSights' Andy Li says a cyclical view implies a 'dramatic price decline may well be in the cards'; Barron's called memory stocks 'agonizingly cheap' (Dow Jones (MarketWatch via Morningstar); Barron's, 2026-11-20)

Competitor leadership: Samsung promoted Hwang Sang-joon, who led its DRAM and HBM development, to president and head of the memory business; co-CEO Jun Young-hyun keeps the wider chip division and will focus on foundry, and process chief Lee Jong-myeong becomes the chip division's CTO (Reuters (via StreetInsider), 2026-11-20)

Competitors: SK hynix will convert ¥129B (~$810M) of Kioxia-linked convertible bonds into shares, becoming Kioxia's largest indirect shareholder at 14.1% (Toshiba 10.46%); it says it has no plans to buy more, sell, or expand its role in Kioxia's management (Yonhap, 2026-11-20)

Spot pricing (TrendForce / DRAMeXchange, third-party, 20 Nov GMT+8): DDR5 16Gb $60.667 (flat), DDR4 16Gb $78.625 (−0.16%), DDR4 8Gb $43.75 (−0.39%); DDRWatcher (est.) has DDR4 spot down 1.4% w/w (fifth weekly drop) and DDR5 +0.5% w/w, with no contract reset yet. VDURA says 30TB SSD prices are down 5–15% across the board, the first substantial cut since summer 2025 (TrendForce / DRAMeXchange; DDRWatcher; Blocks & Files, 2026-11-20)

Contract vs spot (KB Securities, third-party est., 20 Nov): KB sees 2027 DRAM demand +25% against supply +18%, with key customers receiving only ~70% of what they need, and forecasts Samsung/SK hynix contract DRAM ASPs +40% and NAND +30% in 2027; it says DRAM and NAND spot fell ~5% and ~20% in the past month while contract prices kept rising, putting the spot–contract gap above 20%, and calls chip-stock pessimism 'near its peak'. Samsung and SK hynix were down ~4% and ~5% in Korean pre-market trading after the US chip sell-off (Edaily (KB Securities estimate); Financial News, 2026-11-20)

Lynx Equity (KC Rajkumar) named Micron its top semiconductor pick and kept a $1,325 target, calling the stock 'ridiculously cheap' at ~2.3x his calendar-2028 EPS estimate; he argues slower data-centre permitting does not mean weaker DRAM/NAND demand (Investing.com, 2026-11-19)

MU fell 2.10% on 19 Nov to close at $690.44 (from $705.27; range $689.27–$760.00, ~35M shares), its sixth straight decline and lowest close since 6 Nov, after opening near $740 on Anthropic's Nasdaq debut and reversing as AI and chip stocks sold off (S&P 500 −2.0%, Nasdaq −2.25%, SOX −2.4%; Nvidia −3.3%; AMD −7.7% on a Hunterbrook short report on China exports); MU traded ~$678.70 after hours (Nasdaq.com, 6:39 pm ET) (Nasdaq.com / Reuters (via Investing.com), 2026-11-19)

Taiwan labour: the Micron Taoyuan union says Micron made no new offer at the 17 Nov mediation, so members vote on the current proposal from 21 to 24 Nov, ahead of the second mediation on 26 Nov; Micron said it respects employees' rights and will keep talking through existing channels (TaiSounds, 2026-11-19)

Fabs/HBM: Micron moved the first process tool into the cleanroom of its US$7B Singapore HBM advanced-packaging facility on 19 Nov, with initial output expected in early 2027; TrendForce notes the Taoyuan union will put Micron's proposal to a member vote ahead of a second mediation session on 26 Nov (Singapore EDB; TrendForce, 2026-11-19)

Export policy: with the new BIS rules in force from 19 Nov, TSMC has told affected Chinese chip designers to halt orders at 16nm and below unless they obtain US licences, generally limiting them to 28/40nm without HBM or advanced packaging (sources); the FT reports TSMC and Samsung have also paused some shipments to Chinese customers (Reuters (via Investing.com), 2026-11-19)

Earnings date confirmed: Micron will hold its FQ1 FY27 earnings call on Thursday 17 Dec 2026 at 2:30 pm Mountain time (4:30 pm ET; 05:30 SGT Fri 18 Dec), replacing the third-party 16 Dec / 23 Dec estimates. The guide is revenue $60–63B and non-GAAP EPS $38.15 ± $1.00 (Micron press release (GlobeNewswire), 2026-11-19)

Anthropic debut: ANT opened at $111.50 against the $83 IPO price, reached $115 (+38.6%) and closed up 17.1% (Reuters), but the rally faded across AI hardware as investors sold chip names to fund ANT positions (MarketWatch). Dashboard arithmetic, not a company figure: Micron's ~$1.0B Class N purchase at $83 would be marked up ~17% (~$170M, unrealised) at that close (Reuters (via Investing.com); MarketWatch, 2026-11-19)

Customer LTAs: Apple is in final-stage talks with Samsung on a 4–5-year DRAM supply deal starting 1H27 (minimum volumes, market-based pricing), after reportedly signing one with SK hynix, a break from its short-contract buying; the paper contrasts Micron's stricter SCA terms (price floors/ceilings, cash deposits, take-or-pay) (The Korea Herald, 2026-11-19)

Spot pricing (TrendForce / DRAMeXchange, third-party, 19 Nov GMT+8): DRAM spot 'no demand inquiries at all'; DDR5 16Gb $60.667 (+0.28%), DDR4 16Gb $78.75 (−0.25%), DDR4 8Gb $43.921 (−0.25%). NAND: TLC 512Gb wafer spot $14.20 (−24% m/m) and 1Tb −14%; TrendForce (est.) now sees overall NAND contract prices −0–5% q/q in 1Q27 as lower Chinese CSP enterprise-SSD demand offsets North America (TrendForce / DRAMeXchange; MoneyToday, 2026-11-19)

RBC Capital (Srini Pajjuri) reiterated Outperform and a $1,500 target after an investor meeting with Micron IR (Satya Kumar): management expects tighter industry supply in 2027–28, is not worried about de-spec'ing, sounded confident SCAs are enforceable, and intends to return 100% of excess cash over time, mainly via buybacks; RBC calls the pullback an opportunity (MU ~4.2x CY27E EPS, RBC est.) (Investing.com / MarketBeat, 2026-11-18)

MU fell 1.00% on 18 Nov to close at $705.27 (from $712.42; range $687.34–$722.95, ~27M shares), its fifth straight decline, giving back a ~4.8% after-hours gain from Nvidia's results as NAND-glut worries (GF Securities) kept memory names under pressure (SanDisk −2.6% ahead of its 8-for-1 split); MU traded ~$714 after hours (Nasdaq.com, 6:38 pm ET) (Nasdaq.com / 24/7 Wall St., 2026-11-18)

Management comments: at the TomorrowX Summit in Austin, CEO Sanjay Mehrotra said demand is robust, supply tight and pricing constructive, that calendar 2027 and 2028 will be even tighter than 2026, and that 75% of Micron's 2027 output is already sold out with 2028 commitments under discussion; Micron cited 26 supply and collaboration agreements with $32B of upfront cash and financial commitments, said it still works closely with Nvidia, and reiterated that shareholder returns step up after CHIPS restrictions lapse on 9 Dec (Investing.com (event transcript) / Seeking Alpha, 2026-11-18)

DRAM/HBM pricing outlook (TrendForce Seoul roadshow, third-party est.): conventional DRAM ASPs +10–15% q/q in 4Q26, then slowing to +5–10%, +3–8%, 0–5% and 0–5% q/q through 1Q–4Q27; HBM4 seen at $3–5.5/Gb in 2027 vs ≥$2.05/Gb in 2026, with HBM4E discussed above $5/Gb (Chosun Biz / FXBus (TrendForce estimate), 2026-11-18)

Spot pricing (TrendForce weekly, third-party): DRAM buyers stay on the sidelines even as some suppliers offer lower prices; DDR4 8Gb 3200 fell 1.43% w/w to $44.25 (17 Nov) while branded DDR5 held steady; NAND sellers are cutting prices to clear inventory and the NAND spot–contract gap now exceeds 20%. 18 Nov session: DDR5 16Gb $60.50 (+0.28%), DDR4 16Gb $78.95 (−0.22%), DDR4 8Gb $44.03 (−0.50%) (TrendForce / DRAMeXchange; Newspim, 2026-11-18)

Competitors: Korean coverage of Nvidia's results notes $203B of its $390B supply commitments fall in FY28; Samsung's Q3 filing says demand keeps outrunning its output increases and it has long-term memory deals with 10 large customers (10 more in talks), while SK hynix says DRAM/HBM output through 2029 is booked and is adding HBM4 packaging/test capacity for 1H27 (etnews) (Aju News / Financial News (Korea), 2026-11-18)

China competitor: CXMT CEO Mark Cao said at its 17 Nov Q3 briefing that it has signed long-term DRAM supply agreements with several tier-one customers, while its 4F² DRAM production is still awaiting customer validation (DigiTimes, 2026-11-18)

Anthropic IPO: priced at $83 a share, above the $70–78 range (sources told CNBC; ~$1.4–1.5T valuation), with Nasdaq trading (ANT) due 19 Nov; Micron's ~$1.0B Class N purchase in the private placement is at the IPO price (CNBC, 2026-11-18)

Export policy: CNBC reports the new BIS AI-chip licence rule puts Southeast Asia's data-centre build-out (Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia) at risk; the rule targets AI processors and servers rather than memory directly (CNBC, 2026-11-18)

MU slipped 0.92% on 17 Nov to close at $712.42 (from $719.02; range $666.88–$726.98, ~30.9M shares), its fourth straight decline, after falling as much as ~7% intraday on a GF Securities NAND downgrade, the DRAM antitrust ruling and a report of an NSA network outage; the S&P 500 posted its lowest close since July. After Nvidia's results MU traded about 4.8% higher after hours (~$746.5, Nasdaq.com, 6:40 pm ET) (Nasdaq.com / CNBC, 2026-11-17)

Largest HBM customer: Nvidia FQ3 FY27 revenue was $115.8B (+103% y/y; data centre $107.6B) vs ~$109.1B expected (LSEG, est.), with a FQ4 guide of $130B ±3% (no China data-centre compute assumed) and FY28 growth raised to ~75%; supply and capacity commitments rose to $390B from $279B, mainly on multi-year memory procurement (CFO commentary). Vera Rubin NVL72 is shipping. Nvidia rose ~2–4% after hours (Nvidia / CNBC, 2026-11-17)

NAND outlook (GF Securities, third-party est.): GF cut its 2027 NAND price forecast and now sees prices flat in 1Q27 then falling in each of the next three quarters, with double-digit smartphone/PC unit declines, slower enterprise-SSD orders and supply bit growth of ~28% in 2027 and ~30% in 2028; it sees SanDisk most exposed and Micron cushioned by DRAM/HBM (TIKR (GF Securities estimate), 2026-11-17)

NAND pricing (TrendForce, third-party est.): NAND spot prices fell ~20% in two weeks as Chinese traders cut inventory and YMTC pushes commodity output; BofA (est.) puts 512Gb wafers at $14.30 (−32% q/q) and 1Tb at $24.90 (−19%) and sees phone/PC NAND contracts −5–10% q/q in 1Q27, while TrendForce still forecasts enterprise SSD contract prices +15–20% q/q in 4Q26 (TrendForce / Seoul Economic Daily (BofA estimate), 2026-11-17)

DRAM spot (TrendForce / DRAMeXchange, third-party, 17 Nov GMT+8): DDR5 16Gb 4800/5600 session avg $60.333 (flat), DDR4 16Gb 3200 $79.125 (−0.32%), DDR4 8Gb 3200 $44.25 (−0.24%); Digital Times notes DDR5 spot is down 1.9% since 3 Nov and 512Gb TLC NAND wafer spot down 15.5% to $14.267 over the same period (TrendForce / DRAMeXchange; Digital Times, 2026-11-17)

Taiwan labour: Micron and its Taoyuan union resumed talks under city-led mediation on 17 Nov but did not reach agreement, disagreeing over the proposed collective-agreement framework (peace clause, dispute limits, term); the union will put Micron's offer to a member vote and a second mediation is set for 26 Nov. Micron said it will keep talking and follow all legal procedures (Liberty Times, 2026-11-17)

Anthropic IPO: sources told CNBC the IPO is likely to price above its $70–78 range after books closed at 4 pm ET on 17 Nov, with Nasdaq trading (ANT) expected on 19 Nov; Micron is buying about $1.0B of Class N stock in the $26B private placement at the IPO price (CNBC, 2026-11-17)

Largest HBM customer: in his first statement since resigning, Jensen Huang said he would be open to returning as Nvidia CEO if the board asked; Nvidia said it does not plan to reappoint him and took no questions on it on the earnings call, where interim CEO Colette Kress called it 'business as usual' (CNBC / TechCrunch, 2026-11-17)

Competitor HBM: Samsung is reportedly developing custom HBM4E for Meta with a 2nm base die from its own foundry; Nvidia has reportedly asked Samsung, SK hynix and Micron to use TSMC 3nm for its custom HBM base dies, and Micron is said to plan outsourcing base dies starting with HBM4E (industry reports, not confirmed) (TrendForce (citing The Bell / Seoul Economic Daily), 2026-11-17)
